# An ambient enum whose members carry no value cannot receive one back.
#
# `declare enum Color { Red, Green }` says which members exist and not what
# they are; TypeScript numbers them 0, 1 when it emits the object, but the
# .d.ts is the only file the importer reads and it does not say so. So the 0
# the function returns matches no member, and the key fails naming the enum and
# the value rather than resolving to Red by position or surviving as a float.
#
# html under --lang=none cannot call js: at runtime, so a key that cannot be
# folded fails the build.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

! sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
stderr 'is not the value of any member of Color'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import lib "js:./lib"

const c = lib.pick()

component main node {
    if c == lib.Color.Red {
        text(value="red")
    }
}

window {
    main
}
-- lib/index.d.ts --
export declare enum Color {
    Red,
    Green,
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export declare function pick(): Color;
-- lib/index.js --
export const Color = { 0: "Red", Red: 0, 1: "Green", Green: 1 };

export function pick() {
    return Color.Red;
}
